title: Per-Endpoint Parameter Extraction Error Handling
pattern: Request handlers each define their own per-parameter error variants and hand-code missing- or malformed-parameter handling inside individual endpoints, instead of a single dispatcher-level extraction layer that reports parameter errors uniformly.
why_bad: Parameter error handling is scattered and duplicated across every endpoint, each with slightly different variants, messages and status codes. Handling the missing-parameter case once at the dispatcher (or in a typed extractor) removes these errors from service methods entirely: handlers receive already-validated parameters.
detection: Multiple endpoint or service methods that each look up raw request parameters by name and wrap each failed lookup in an endpoint-specific error variant (`MissingId`, `MissingQty`, ...), rather than declaring typed parameters extracted by the framework or a shared dispatcher.
counterexample: Endpoints where a missing parameter triggers fallback behavior rather than rejection, and single one-off handlers with genuinely endpoint-specific validation.
source: John Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design*, Section 10.7, pp. 82–83.
